mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an easing monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate above 4.6% within a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which precedes corporate earnings slowdowns and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when UNRATE rises >0.2pp in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenue expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline for 3 months, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During strong industrial production growth (INDPRO > 102.0), S&P 500 experiences positive returns over 60 trading days as corporate profits rise, but this effect is inactive during low industrial growth periods.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when INDPRO > 102.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1250.0 thousand units in the most recent month signals housing sector contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when HOUST < 1250.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) and rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 4.5%) indicates tightening monetary policy coinciding with labor weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS >4.0% AND UNRATE >4.5%, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL annual change > 2.5%), the Federal Reserve maintains restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as real capital costs rise.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annual change > 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.
